stem: Fourth generation of computers started with the invention of
explanation: Fourth-generation computers (1971–present) began with the invention of the VLSI microprocessor, integrating the entire CPU onto a single silicon chip.

option_feedback.reason: Vacuum tubes were used in first-generation computers.
Integrated circuits (ICs) marked the third generation of computers.
Artificial intelligence is associated with fifth-generation computing.

current_mapping.description: classify programming languages into low-level (machine and assembly) and high-level (procedural and object-oriented) languages;

stem: A programming language that is easy for humans to understand is called
explanation: High-level programming languages (such as Python, Java, and C++) use English-like words and familiar mathematical notation, making them easy for humans to read, write, and understand.

option_feedback.reason: Machine language consists of raw binary 0s and 1s, which is directly understood by the CPU but very difficult for humans.
Assembly language is a low-level symbolic language using hardware-specific mnemonics.
Low-level languages (machine and assembly) are machine-oriented and difficult for humans to read.

current_mapping.description: illustrate the Von Neumann Architecture using a block diagram;

stem: Which of the following components of processor will perform the operation `5 + 10`?
explanation: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) inside the processor executes all mathematical calculations (such as addition `5 + 10`, subtraction, multiplication, and division) as well as logical comparisons.

option_feedback.reason: The input unit accepts raw data from external input peripherals.
The Control Unit (CU) directs instruction fetching and decoding and issues timing signals rather than computing sums.
The Memory Unit (MU) stores instructions and data temporarily rather than performing arithmetic.

current_mapping.description: compare the types of primary memory, i.e., Random Access Memory (RAM) and Read Only Memory (ROM);

stem: When compared with Static RAM (SRAM), which of the following is TRUE about Dynamic RAM (DRAM)?

options.C: DRAM is a type of non-volatile memory.
options.D: DRAM needs to be refreshed periodically.

explanation: Dynamic RAM (DRAM) stores each bit as an electrical charge in a tiny capacitor that leaks charge over milliseconds, so it must be recharged (refreshed) thousands of times per second.

option_feedback.reason: SRAM (used for CPU cache) is much faster than DRAM because it uses flip-flop latches that do not need refreshing.
DRAM is simpler (1 transistor + 1 capacitor per bit) and much cheaper per gigabyte than SRAM.
Both DRAM and SRAM are volatile memories that lose their contents when power is turned off.

stem: Which of the following is TRUE about serial ports?

options.A: They transmit one bit at a time.
options.B: They are faster than parallel ports.
options.C: They are also called line printer (LPT) ports.
options.D: They are largest ports on the rear of computer system.

explanation: A serial port (COM port) transmits data sequentially one bit at a time over a single data communication wire.

option_feedback.reason: Legacy RS-232 serial ports transmit 1 bit at a time and are slower over short distances than 8-bit parallel ports.
Line Printer (`LPT`) ports are 25-pin parallel ports, whereas serial ports are `COM` (communication) ports.
Serial ports (9-pin DB-9) are smaller than 25-pin DB-25 parallel printer ports.

current_mapping.description: illustrate the system bus and its types, including data bus, address bus and control bus, along with their roles in computer architecture using a diagram;

stem: Which of the following provides connectivity between central processing unit (CPU) and memory ONLY?
explanation: The unidirectional Address Bus carries physical memory addresses from the CPU to main memory (RAM) to identify the specific storage location to read or write.

option_feedback.reason: A serial port connects external peripheral devices.
The Control Bus connects the CPU with both memory and all I/O controllers.
A parallel port connects external peripherals such as printers.

stem:
The keys on a computer keyboard are divided into five groups.
Which of the key groups encircled below is the 'Function key group' on a standard keyboard?
explanation: Group A encircles the top row of keys labelled `F1` through `F12`, which is the Function Key group used to perform special shortcut commands in software applications.

option_feedback.reason: Group B points to the keyboard lock status indicator LEDs (`Num Lock`, `Caps Lock`, `Scroll Lock`).
Group C encircles the four directional arrow (cursor control) keys.
Group D encircles the right-hand Numeric Keypad (`0–9` and arithmetic operators).

stem: Which of the following devices is suitable for producing large drawings or images such as plans of buildings or blue prints of complex machines like an aircraft?
explanation: A plotter is a specialised large-format vector output device used by architects and engineers (with CAD software) to print wide-format architectural blueprints, maps, and aircraft/machine schematics.

option_feedback.reason: A dot-matrix printer is a low-resolution impact printer used for carbon-copy invoices and receipts.
A standard desktop inkjet printer prints letter/A4 documents and photos rather than large-scale engineering blueprints.
A standard laser printer prints office text documents on standard sheet sizes.

current_mapping.description: distinguish among the memory measuring units such as bits, bytes, kilobytes, megabytes, and gigabytes in computer memory;

stem:
Each alphabet, symbol or number on a standard keyboard can be represented by an ASCII number. One ASCII number occupies one byte of memory.
How many bits are required to store the word **STAR** in computer memory?
explanation: The word `STAR` consists of 4 characters (`S`, `T`, `A`, `R`). Each ASCII character occupies $1\text{ byte} = 8\text{ bits}$, so storing 4 characters requires $4 \times 8 = 32\text{ bits}$.

option_feedback.reason: 4 is the number of bytes (characters), not the number of bits ($4 \times 8 = 32\text{ bits}$).
8 bits equals only 1 byte (enough for just 1 character).
16 bits equals 2 bytes (enough for only 2 characters).

current_mapping.description: describe primary and secondary storage devices based on location, cost, capacity, access time, data processing method, and storage technology such as semiconductor (SSD), magnetic (HDD), and optical;

stem:
The data storage part of a hard disk consists of metallic circular platters.
Consider the image of a hard disk platter.
The portion of hard disk platter shaded and marked with X is known as
explanation: A magnetic hard disk platter is organised into concentric rings (tracks) and wedge-shaped subdivisions (sectors); the shaded arc segment marked X is a sector.

option_feedback.reason: A track is an entire full concentric circle around the platter.
The read/write head is the electromagnetic actuator arm that reads data from the spinning platter.
The hard disk controller is the circuit board managing the drive.

stem:
Binary, decimal, octal and hexadecimal are the number systems widely used in the field of computer science.
The number $(112)_8$ is an example of
explanation: The subscript base (radix) `8` in $(112)_8$ indicates that the number is written in the base-8 (octal) number system, which uses digits `0` through `7`.

option_feedback.reason: Binary numbers have a base subscript of `2` and only contain digits `0` and `1`.
Decimal numbers have a base subscript of `10`.
Hexadecimal numbers have a base subscript of `16`.

stem: If the decimal number $167$ is stored in computer memory, then what is the binary equivalent of this decimal number?
The hexadecimal digit `C` is equal to decimal number
explanation: In the base-16 (hexadecimal) number system, `A` = 10, `B` = 11, `C` = 12, `D` = 13, `E` = 14, and `F` = 15.

option_feedback.reason: Decimal 10 is represented by the hexadecimal digit `A`.
Decimal 11 is represented by the hexadecimal digit `B`.
Decimal 13 is represented by the hexadecimal digit `D`.

stem: How many binary digits (bits) are required to represent hexadecimal number **ABC**?
explanation: Each hexadecimal digit corresponds to exactly 4 binary bits ($2^4 = 16$). Since `ABC` has 3 hexadecimal digits, it requires $3 \times 4 = 12\text{ bits}$ (`1010 1011 1100`).

option_feedback.reason: 3 is the number of hexadecimal digits, not the number of binary bits.
6 bits only represent 1.5 hexadecimal digits.
24 bits would represent 6 hexadecimal digits ($6 \times 4 = 24$).

current_mapping.description: describe the purpose of the following application software: a. word processor, b. spreadsheet, c. database management, d. presentation/ desktop publication, e. communication, f. entertainment;

stem:
Shanaya is an Associate Director in an organisation. She has to give a presentation in a meeting. The presentation includes text, graphics, animation and a movie clip.
The most suitable software for Shanaya to give presentation is
explanation: Microsoft PowerPoint is presentation application software specifically designed to create multimedia slide shows combining text, graphics, animations, and embedded video clips.

option_feedback.reason: MS Excel is spreadsheet software used for numerical calculations and data analysis.
MS Word is word-processing software used for creating text documents and reports.
MS Access is relational database management software.

stem: Aryan is working on MS Word file and he wants to know the total number of pages in the file. The bar that will help him for this purpose is
explanation: In Microsoft Word, the Status Bar at the bottom of the application window displays the current page number, total page count, and word count.

option_feedback.reason: The Menu Bar lists top-level command menus.
The Toolbar holds icon shortcuts for common formatting actions.
The Title Bar at the top displays the document filename.

stem: If any file/ folder is minimised in Windows, then which of the following would be the best option to find the minimised file/ folder instantly?
explanation: When an open window, file, or folder is minimised in Microsoft Windows, its icon/button remains docked on the horizontal Taskbar (marked `D`) at the bottom of the screen so it can be restored with a single click.

option_feedback.reason: Arrow A points to the Recycle Bin icon, which stores deleted files.
Arrow B points to the My Documents desktop folder icon.
Arrow C points to the Start button, which opens the Start Menu.

stem:
Akram has deleted a PowerPoint presentation file accidently.
He can restore the deleted file from
explanation: In Microsoft Windows, files accidentally deleted from the hard drive are moved to the Recycle Bin, from which they can be restored to their original location.

option_feedback.reason: Control Panel is used to configure system hardware, software, and user settings.
My Computer (This PC) displays connected disk drives and partitions.
My Documents is the default user folder for saving personal files, not a trash recovery folder.

stem: Which of the following print layouts are used to print text on a horizontal page?
explanation: Landscape orientation rotates the page horizontally so that the page width is greater than its height.

option_feedback.reason: Portrait orientation prints the page vertically (taller than it is wide).
Normal is a margin preset or view mode, not a horizontal page orientation.
Legal is a paper size ($8.5 \times 14\text{ inches}$), not a page orientation.

stem: You can run a slideshow in PowerPoint using
explanation: Pressing the `F5` function key in Microsoft PowerPoint starts the presentation slide show from the first slide.

option_feedback.reason: `F6` cycles focus among different panes in the PowerPoint window.
`F7` launches the Spelling checker dialog.
`ESC` ends an active slide show and returns to the editing view.

stem: Which of the following is an example of an operating system?
explanation: Microsoft Windows is a Graphical User Interface (GUI) operating system (system software) that manages computer hardware and software resources.

option_feedback.reason: Microsoft Office is an integrated suite of application software.

current_mapping.description: explain the following types of system software: a. operating system, b. device drivers, c. utility programs, d. language processors;

stem: GUI stands for
explanation: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface, which allows users to interact with an operating system through visual windows, icons, menus, and a pointer.

option_feedback.reason: 'Geographical' is incorrect; the 'G' stands for 'Graphical'.
'Giga Byte' is a memory unit, not part of GUI.
'Interrupt' is a CPU signal; the 'I' stands for 'Interface'.

stem:
There are internal and external commands in disk operating system (DOS).
Which of the following is an external DOS command?
explanation: `DELTREE` (`DELTREE.EXE`) is an external DOS command stored as a separate executable file on disk used to delete a directory and all its subdirectories, whereas `DIR`, `DEL`, and `EXIT` are internal commands built into `COMMAND.COM`.

option_feedback.reason: `DIR` is an internal DOS command used to list directory contents.
`DEL` is an internal DOS command used to delete files.
`EXIT` is an internal DOS command used to close the command interpreter.

stem:
Kazim is using disk operating system (DOS). He wants to delete all the files in the current directory.
The DOS command he should use for this purpose is
explanation: In MS-DOS, `DEL *.*` (or `DEL*.*`) uses the `*.*` wildcard to delete all files with any name and any extension inside the current working directory.

option_feedback.reason: `DEL` without a filename or wildcard argument produces a missing parameter error.
`DELTREE` removes an entire directory tree including subdirectories rather than just the files in the current directory.
`DELFILES` is not a valid MS-DOS command.

current_mapping.description: compare system software and application software, highlighting their roles in a computer system;

stem: Which of the following is an example of application software?
explanation: MS Word is application software used by end users to create and format text documents, whereas Anti-virus, Screen saver, and MS Windows are system software.

option_feedback.reason: An antivirus program is a system utility program.
A screen saver is a system utility program.
MS Windows is an operating system (system software).
